name: 6-APB
addictionPotential: moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
summary: A stimulant, empathogen and analog of MDA. Typically more visual than MDMA or MDA, as well as having a much longer onset and duration. Users often report a slightly more psychedelic headspace as well. Commonly sold as an alternative to MDMA and MDA.
advisory: It is not recommended to consume more than 200mg in a night
doseBasis: NOTE: It is not recommended to consume more than 200mg in a night

subjectiveEffects.name: Light to moderate visuals are reported with most users

pharmacology.text: 6-APB acts as a serotonin–norepinephrine–dopamine releasing agent (SNDRA), with EC50 values for monoamine release of 36 nM for serotonin, 14 nM for norepinephrine, and 10 nM for dopamine in rat brain synaptosomes.
pharmacology.kind: Serotonin–norepinephrine–dopamine releasing agent; Serotonin 5-HT2 receptor agonist; Entactogen; Stimulant; Psychedelic

uses.text: It falls under the category of research chemicals, sometimes called "legal highs" if uncontrolled. 6-APB was first described in the scientific literature in 2000 and emerged as a novel designer drug in 2010.

sideEffects.text: Acute psychosis has been associated with recreational use of 6-APB in combination with the synthetic cannabinoid JWH-122.

fact.en: Its street name benzofury comes from its benzofuran ring. It was first described in the scientific literature in 2000, ten years before it appeared as a designer drug.
